title: I’m lost…
text:
Had such high hopes for this app after hearing it was a good alternative to PhotoRoom, which is the best ai photo editing app out there (especially for resellers). But I didn’t want to sign up for the free three day trial like it tries to get you to when first opening the app. So it instead said I had “10 cutouts” left when I went to remove the background of a photo. However, it just kept spinning and spinning, like it was working, but nothing ever happened. When I closed out of it and opened another photo to remove its background, same thing happened, but this time it said I had “9 cutouts remaining.” Where’s the first one? And when I again tried the bg remover, it said I had “8 cutouts remaining,” despite never seeing a single one!
PhotoRoom has SOME limits to how many times you’re able to edit photos (I use it at least 50-75 times a month without any issues), but I know I couldn’t reach the limit and I use it daily. The reviews for PixelCut are a 4.7 rating, but I don’t know how; I can’t be the only one experiencing this bs.

title: Pixelcut Review
text: I got this app in 2023 for fun/creative projects. There is nothing wrong with it at all, and I used to use it all of the time. I just happen to prefer more professional graphic design/editing services like Canva and Photoshop. Also, the second you log in, it asks you about subscriptions and features you need to buy, and I just like a chill editing app that lets you choose if you want the premium features or not. I would recommend it if you are new to graphic design and need a simple, fun, and helpful program to get you started.

title: Sad Purchase
text:
★★☆☆☆

I really wanted to like Pixelcut, especially the feature that allows you to place your clothing or products on AI-generated models. The concept is excellent, but the execution has been disappointing.

My biggest concern is the lack of diversity in the available models. I have not found models who reflect me, and that matters when you are trying to visualize or market clothing authentically. A much broader range of skin tones, ages, body types, and overall representation is needed. For me, this is a major issue and honestly would have affected my decision to purchase the subscription had I noticed it beforehand.

The second problem is even more frustrating. When I upload one of my custom jackets and place it on a model, Pixelcut sometimes changes the actual jacket. It may add details, alter embellishments, or modify parts of the design that are not on the original garment. Since I create one-of-a-kind pieces, I need the photograph of the jacket to remain accurate. I cannot advertise something that looks different from what I am actually selling.

I have not found a reliable way to tell the program, “Do not change my garment. Only place this exact item on the model.”

Unfortunately, after paying approximately $89, I feel that I wasted my money. The model feature could be a game changer, but only if Pixelcut offers much more diverse representation and gives users a true product-preservation option that prevents AI from redesigning the item being photographed.
